brief: GS sales compilation (Adam Crook) covering four client questions plus a trade package. Fed/CPI: a hotter CPI print pushed December hike pricing just above a full hike and shifted 2027 pricing toward front-loaded Q1 hikes; terminal pricing reached roughly 4.75% versus GS Economics' updated call for a third 25bp hike in March (after Sept and Dec), with desks seeing adjustment hikes stopping near 4.25-4.5% and neutral at 3.75-4%. Data-centre policy: Democratic state wins campaigned on utility-bill affordability tied to data-centre build-out; states likely to tighten regulation hold roughly 45% of planned US capacity (Texas about 25%), but GS views this as a timing risk to construction, not a capacity risk, since hyperscaler demand stays strong and many operators already meet likely requirements. Trades: reduced Gulf-escalation risk puts oil in an $85-105 range skewed lower, so GS funds high-beta and EM-carry longs via EUR/CHF instead of USD, expressed through EUR-funded FX binaries, HUF/SAGB EM-rate receivers, Brent vol relative value, and EURUSD lower versus equities higher. Brazil: investors have largely exited the trade after a disappointing fiscal package; EWZ is down 23% since the election with a $1.5bn redemption overhang still to clear by mid-December. Separately, GS projects 2027 Eurozone core inflation at 2.9%, headline 4.4%, the highest since Q3-23.
